newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran MPs give province status to 1994 riot city.
newsitem.headline: Iran MPs give province status to 1994 riot city.

text.p: Iran's parliament on Wednesday agreed to raise the city of Qazvin to the status of a province, reversing a 1994 vote that led to major riots in the industrial centre, Iranian media said.
Deputies approved by a large margin a government bill setting up Qazvin province, which will include the city 150 km (90 miles) northwest of Tehran and several nearby districts, media reports said.

The move boosts Qazvin's economic and political influence and creates more jobs in the city that saw several days of rioting in August 1994. Banks, government buildings and shops were attacked and set on fire after deputies narrowly defeated an earlier bill to separate it from Zanjan province.

Qazvin, with a population of 750,000, is a main industrial city and lies on the highway from the Turkish and Azerbaijani borders to Tehran used for overland imports. It was Iran's capital for several decades in the 16th century.
The law creating the new province has to be approved by the clergy-based Guardian Council, which vets parliamentary decisions for accordance with Islam and the Constitution.
